insights.title: A 146-year registry of Gujarat corporate India
insights.detail: The file holds 222.9k companies registered with the Registrar of Companies, Ahmedabad, between 1880 and 2026 across 16 administrative fields. All records carry a state code of Gujarat, making this a single-state census of corporate registrations rather than a sample.

insights.title: Identity keys are pristine - no duplicates at all
insights.detail: Despite 222.9k records there are 0 duplicate rows and 0 repeated CINs, so every company appears exactly once. Cleaning effort can therefore focus on content issues rather than identity resolution.

insights.title: 23.23% of rows miss ALL detail fields together - and the pattern is NOT random
insights.detail: 51.8k rows lack every company-detail field (category, class, subcategory, capitals, listing status, NIC code) simultaneously, while identifier fields are 100% populated. Block-missingness is strongly associated with observed variables: it reaches 36.1% for companies registered in 2016-2026 but is ~0% before 2001 (chi2 era: p < 0.001, Cramer's V = 0.384), and Active companies miss more (28.6%) than struck-off ones (7.5%) (V = 0.2188). The mechanism is therefore MAR/MNAR with an administrative cause - recent registrations in the extract simply have not had their detail fields populated - rather than pure MCAR.

insights.title: Corporate capital is extremely right-skewed
insights.detail: Authorised capital has a median of ₹1.00 L against a mean of ₹11.16 Cr (skewness 163.291), with values from ₹0 to ₹190,000.00 Cr. The coefficient of variation exceeds 7,000%, so all capital analysis uses log10 scale and robust statistics (median, IQR, MAD) per the course's descriptive-summary module.

insights.title: The top 1.0% of companies hold 93.26% of paid-up capital
insights.detail: The Lorenz curve shows extreme inequality (Gini = 0.9918): a handful of mega-companies dominate Gujarat's corporate capital, while the median company is capitalised at just ₹1.00 L. This mirrors the national picture where a few large listed groups hold most subscribed capital.

insights.title: Authorised and paid-up capital move together (R2 = 0.5925)
insights.detail: On the log10 scale, paid-up capital rises almost proportionally with authorised capital: Pearson r = 0.7697 (Spearman rho = 0.765, robust to heavy tails). The OLS slope of 0.8743 implies that a 10x increase in authorised capital is associated with roughly a 10^0.87 = ~7.5x increase in paid-up capital - authorisation tracks, but does not guarantee, actual capitalisation.

insights.title: Company class and legal status are significantly dependent
insights.detail: A chi-square test of the class x status crosstab gives chi2 = 2,499 (p < 0.001); Cramer's V = 0.0854 indicates a modest but reliable association given the huge sample. One Person Companies are the healthiest cohort (87.5% active, only 12.3% struck off), whereas public companies show the weakest active share (58.6% active, 30.4% struck off / in process) - consistent with many old public companies being defunct shells.
insights.evidence: chi2=2499.09; p=0.0; cramers_v=0.0854; OPC active=87.5%; Public active=58.6%

insights.title: Registrations exploded to a peak of 22.4k in 2025
insights.detail: Annual registrations grew from 5.3k in 2015 to 22.4k in 2025 (CAGR 2025%, 2015-2025), with every year since 2021 exceeding 13,000. The post-2020 acceleration is consistent with SPICe+ online incorporation and start-up formalisation; 2026 is already at 0 registrations by June, on pace for another record. March dominates the calendar pattern (financial year-end rush) while November is the quietest month, confirming seasonality.

insights.title: 18050 capital outliers on the log scale - and they are real giants
insights.detail: Tukey's 1.5*IQR fences on log10 capital flag 11.27% of companies as high-side outliers, led by mega-cap names whose paid-up capital reaches ₹153,125.00 Cr. Zero-capital entries (10.9k companies with ₹0 paid-up) form the low-side special case requiring separate treatment.

insights.title: Manufacturing leads with 34.9% of classified companies
insights.detail: Among the 165.5k companies with a known NIC code, the top sectors are Manufacturing (57,769), Professional & scientific (29,682) and Wholesale & retail trade (17,276) - a signature of Gujarat's industry-and-entrepreneurship-led economy. The 5-digit NIC codes also demonstrate a clean nominal-scale mapping to the 21 one-letter NIC-2008 sections used for grouped analysis.
insights.evidence: top=Manufacturing (57769), Professional & scientific (29682), Wholesale & retail trade (17276); classified_total=165485
